info.name: Veriqon QR Menu & Loyalty Platform API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the multi-tenant QR Menu & Loyalty backend: Super Admin, Restaurant Owner Dashboard, Public QR Menu & Ordering, Waiter Panel, and Customer Auth & Loyalty.

How to use:
1. Set `base_url` (collection variable) to your app URL, e.g. http://localhost:8000.
2. Run "Super Admin Login" (after seeding a super admin) or any login request — tokens and IDs are saved automatically into collection variables by each request's test script, so later requests in the same folder work without manual copy/paste.
3. Folders are ordered to tell a working story: Super Admin creates a restaurant -> Owner sets up the menu/tables/staff/loyalty -> Public customer views menu & orders -> Waiter manages the order -> Customer signs up & claims a loyalty offer.

Note: "Waiter - Live Order Stream (SSE)" is a long-lived Server-Sent-Events connection (polls every 2s, closes after ~55s). Postman will show it as a pending request rather than a normal JSON response; this is expected.

request.description: Generic login used by the original /api/me and /api/logout endpoints. Works for any role (super_admin, restaurant, waiter, user) — returns a flat {message, user, token} shape (no success/data envelope).
Seeded by database/seeders/SuperAdminSeeder.php (superadmin@gmail.com / 12345678).
Creates the Restaurant record AND a Restaurant-owner user with a generated temporary password, then emails those credentials to the restaurant's email. name and email are required.

exec: console.log('Check storage/logs/laravel.log (or your mail driver) for the generated owner password.');

request.description: Flips active<->inactive. A disabled restaurant's owner/staff logins and public menu/ordering are blocked on their very next request.
Cascades: deletes the owner user account too, and (via DB foreign keys) categories, products, tables, orders, loyalty offers for this restaurant.
total_restaurants, active_restaurants, inactive_restaurants, total_orders, orders_today, pending_orders.

Use the email/temporary password from the "Create Restaurant" step (check your mail log) — set owner_password manually the first time, or change it via Change Password below and update the collection variable.
All fields are optional (sometimes): name, email, phone.

formdata.description: Laravel method-spoofing: file uploads must be multipart, which HTML/Postman cannot send as PUT directly.

request.description: Sent as POST + _method=PUT because file uploads require multipart/form-data. Pick a logo file in the 'logo' field before sending.
name is required. description, sorting_order, status (active|inactive, defaults to active) are optional.

formdata.description: Optional. Enable and pick a file to upload a product image.

request.description: name and price are required. category_id, description, image, status (active|inactive|out_of_stock, defaults active) are optional. Sent as multipart since image upload is supported.
Sent as POST + _method=PUT for the same reason as the logo upload above.
status: active | inactive | out_of_stock. Reflected instantly on the public menu.
Returns qr_token and a qr_target_url (e.g. {app_url}/r/{slug}?table={qr_token}) — feed that URL into any QR-image library to print it. label must be unique per restaurant.
Invalidates the old printed QR code (e.g. a lost/compromised table card) and issues a new token.
Generates a temporary password and emails it to the new staff member (check your mail log).

exec: console.log('Check storage/logs/laravel.log (or your mail driver) for the generated staff password.');

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Buy 4 Pizzas Get 1 Free",
  "description": "Applies to any pizza",
  "product_id": {{product_id}},
  "buy_quantity": 4,
  "get_quantity": 1
}

request.description: title and buy_quantity are required. product_id is optional (omit/null to apply to any product) and, if given, must belong to this restaurant. get_quantity defaults to 1, is_active defaults to true.
No auth required. Returns only active categories with active (in-stock) products — out-of-stock/inactive items and a disabled restaurant both resolve to 404, never partially shown.

No account required. table_token comes from the table's printed QR code. Instantly becomes visible on the Waiter Panel's order stream. If you're logged in as a customer (send the customer_token as a Bearer header), the order is linked to that account.
Looked up by the unguessable order_number (not the database id) so a guest can poll status without an account.
Accepts either a waiter's credentials or the restaurant owner's (the owner can act as staff too). Use the temporary password emailed when the staff account was created.
Load this once for the initial screen, then subscribe to the live stream below for updates.

Server-Sent Events: polls for new/updated orders every 2 seconds and streams them as `event: order` / `data: {...}`, closing after ~55s (a well-behaved SSE client reconnects automatically). Postman will show this request as pending/streaming rather than returning a normal JSON body — that is expected, not an error. Cancel the request manually when done testing.
Enforces the forward-only workflow: pending -> preparing -> served -> completed. Skipping a step (e.g. pending -> completed) is rejected with 422.
Closes the loyalty verification loop: confirms the customer's one-time code shown on their screen, scoped to this restaurant and rejecting codes already verified/rejected.

Creates the account and emails a verification code. Set customer_email to a unique address before running (e.g. casey+1@example.com) — the account cannot log in until verified. Check your mail log for the code.
Paste the code emailed after sign up into the customer_verification_token collection variable, or directly into this body.
Blocked with 403 until the account's email is verified.
Always returns success (win or lose) so this endpoint cannot be used to enumerate registered emails. Check your mail log for the reset code.
Paste the code emailed by Forgot Password into customer_reset_token first.
Shown directly in the QR menu. Requires a logged-in customer (but not necessarily verified) to view.
Requires a VERIFIED customer account (403 otherwise). Generates a one-time redemption_code — show it to staff, who confirm it via "4. Waiter Panel > Verify Loyalty Redemption".
